counting: 19 top-level classes; 3 nested, anonymous or local classes folded into their owners.

class.bytecode_size.formula: sum of Code attribute lengths of its methods (bytes)
class.bytecode_size.label: Bytecode size
class.bytecode_size.plain: How much compiled code the class has; a rough size measure independent of formatting.

class.complexity.formula: sum over methods of (conditional branch instructions + switch cases + 1)
class.complexity.label: Bytecode complexity
class.complexity.plain: How many decision points the class has in total; approximates cyclomatic complexity from bytecode.

class.cycle_groups.formula: number of cyclic groups (SCCs) containing C
class.cycle_groups.label: Cycle groups
class.cycle_groups.plain: Whether this class is part of a dependency loop.

class.dependency_count.formula: |{referenced types, internal and external, excluding java.lang.*}|
class.dependency_count.label: Distinct dependencies
class.dependency_count.plain: How many different types this class needs to compile.

class.fan_in.label: Fan-in
class.fan_in.plain: How many other classes rely on this class. High fan-in means a change here can affect many places.

class.fan_out.label: Fan-out
class.fan_out.plain: How many other classes this class relies on. High fan-out means it breaks when any of them changes.

class.field_count.label: Fields
class.field_count.plain: How much state the class keeps.

class.layer_violations.formula: |{dependencies from C to a layer C may not use}|
class.layer_violations.label: Layer violations
class.layer_violations.plain: How many times this class reaches into a layer it should not use.

class.max_method_complexity.formula: max over methods of (conditional branches + switch cases + 1)
class.max_method_complexity.label: Most complex method
class.max_method_complexity.plain: How many paths its most complicated method has; each path needs its own test.

class.max_method_size.formula: max Code attribute length over its methods (bytes)
class.max_method_size.label: Largest method
class.max_method_size.plain: The size of its biggest method. Very large methods are hard to read and test.

class.method_count.formula: declared methods excluding synthetic, bridge and lambda methods
class.method_count.label: Methods
class.method_count.plain: How much behaviour the class contains.

package.A.label: Abstractness (A)
package.A.plain: Share of the package that is interfaces or abstract classes.

package.Ca.formula: |{classes outside P that depend on a class in P}|
package.Ca.label: Afferent coupling (Ca)
package.Ca.plain: How many outside classes rely on this package.

package.Ce.formula: |{classes outside P that a class in P depends on}|
package.Ce.label: Efferent coupling (Ce)
package.Ce.plain: How many outside classes this package relies on.

package.D.label: Distance from main sequence (D)
package.D.plain: 0 is balanced. Near 1 means either rigid concrete code that many rely on, or unused abstractions.

package.I.label: Instability (I)
package.I.plain: 0 means many others rely on it and it relies on little (hard to change); 1 means the opposite (easy to change).

package.bytecode_size.formula: sum of class bytecode sizes in P
package.bytecode_size.label: Bytecode size
package.bytecode_size.plain: Total compiled code in the package.

package.cycle_groups.formula: package-level cyclic groups containing P + class-level groups with a member in P
package.cycle_groups.label: Cycle groups
package.cycle_groups.plain: How many dependency loops touch this package.

package.largest_cycle.formula: max size of a class-level cyclic group with a member in P
package.largest_cycle.label: Largest cycle group
package.largest_cycle.plain: Size of the biggest loop touching this package.

package.layer_violations.formula: sum of class layer violations in P
package.layer_violations.label: Layer violations
package.layer_violations.plain: How often code in this package reaches into a forbidden layer.

package.D.note: Not meaningful: the package has no internal dependencies in either direction.
Not meaningful: the package has no internal dependencies in either direction.
